metric: us/run (test-backend-ops perf, GET_ROWS type=q8_0,n=1024,m=151936 token-embedding-lookup shape)

diagnosis.dominant_stall: n/a (per-call blocking host round-trip, not a GPU-side stall)
diagnosis.tools: source read (ggml_sycl_op_get_rows) + comparison against ggml-cuda/getrows.cu reference; measured via test-backend-ops perf, no HW-counter profiling needed since the bottleneck was architectural, not a GPU execution-unit issue; also captured unitrace --metric-query (VectorEngineStalls, ComputeBasic) HW counters before/after for completeness -- both sides show the GET_ROWS kernel itself is tiny and near-idle (EU active <1%, occupancy <3%), confirming the fix's saving was in host-side overhead OUTSIDE the kernel body (not visible to per-kernel GPU counters), consistent with the bottleneck_class above.
diagnosis.notes: The SYCL get_rows implementation, unlike the CUDA reference (ggml-cuda/getrows.cu, which reads src1->data directly as a device pointer with no host-side involvement), did an unconditional host round-trip on EVERY call: sycl::malloc_shared for the row-index buffer, a blocking q.memcpy(...).wait(), a host-side CPU loop bounds-checking every row index, kernel dispatch, then a final q.wait_and_throw() plus sycl::free(). This is pure per-call overhead unrelated to the actual gather work (which the kernel itself already performs correctly, indexing only the requested rows -- the benchmark's inflated GB/s figure for r=1 is a test-harness artifact: op_size() sums the FULL src0 tensor's ggml_nbytes, not the bytes actually gathered, so the reported bandwidth numbers are not meaningful here; the fix targets the measured absolute us/run, which is real). Fix: read src1->data directly as a device pointer inside the kernel (src1 already lives in device-accessible USM as a SYCL backend tensor, exactly like binbcast.cpp already does for its src1), and drop the host validation loop and both blocking waits -- mirroring the CUDA kernel's approach exactly, since it needs no such round-trip either. This removes 2 blocking host<->device syncs and a malloc/free pair from every single GET_ROWS call, which in this workload happens once per decode step (token embedding lookup / output layer selection).

trials.hypothesis: Read the row-index tensor (src1->data) directly as a device USM pointer inside the kernel, removing the malloc_shared+blocking-memcpy+host-bounds-check-loop+wait_and_throw() round-trip that the CUDA reference implementation does not have.
trials.root_cause: Two blocking host<->device syncs (memcpy.wait() and wait_and_throw()) plus a malloc_shared/free pair were paid on every call regardless of how little data was actually gathered. Removing them and reading src1->data directly (already device-accessible, matching binbcast.cpp's existing pattern and the CUDA reference) cuts the fixed per-call overhead. r=1 (decode, single token): 635.22->41.49 us/run (15.31x). r=512 (batched): 798.51->202.03 us/run (3.95x).
